title: Basic Blood Relations
tagline: Year 1 Foundation — Reading family relationships and drawing the family tree

introduction.overview: Blood relation problems describe how people in a family are connected through statements such as "A is the brother of B" or "Pointing to a man, a woman said, he is the son of my mother's only son". You must work out the relationship between two named people. The reliable method is to draw a small family tree, mark each person as male or female where it is known, and then read the answer from the tree.
introduction.placementRelevance: Blood relation questions are commonly asked in the reasoning section of company aptitude rounds. They need no calculation; the challenge is reading the statements precisely and not mixing up the sides of the family.
introduction.realWorldContext: Forms that ask for "next of kin", family-tree charts, inheritance documents and insurance nominee records all rely on correctly reading relationships.

learningObjectives: Know the standard relationship terms and their meanings
Draw a family tree with generation levels and gender marks
Solve "pointing to" statements by working from the speaker
Decode relationships given through symbols such as +, − and ×

requiredTopics: Basic English vocabulary for family relations
prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Generations: grandparents (top), parents, the person and their siblings and cousins, children (bottom). Siblings and cousins sit on the same level.

coreDefinitions: Maternal relations are on the mother's side; paternal relations are on the father's side.
Uncle: the brother of one's father or mother (also the husband of one's aunt). Aunt: the sister of one's father or mother (also the wife of one's uncle).
Cousin: the child of one's uncle or aunt.
Brother-in-law: the brother of one's spouse, or the husband of one's sister. Sister-in-law is defined in the same way.
Nephew and niece: the son and daughter of one's brother or sister.
Grandfather and grandmother: the parents of one's father or mother.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A blood relation puzzle is a small graph. Each statement adds one edge ("parent of", "sibling of", "spouse of"). Once the graph is on paper, the answer is a matter of reading the path between two nodes. The main danger is trying to hold the entire tree in your head instead of drawing it.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Draw a horizontal line for each generation. Put a square for a male, a circle for a female and a short line between spouses. Use a vertical line from the parents to their children. Siblings share the same parent line.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Father's or mother's sibling
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Father's brother = paternal uncle; Father's sister = paternal aunt; Mother's brother = maternal uncle; Mother's sister = maternal aunt
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Name the side and the gender.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Spouse's relatives
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Spouse's father = father-in-law; spouse's mother = mother-in-law; spouse's brother or sister's husband = brother-in-law

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Pointing statements
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Start from the speaker, work outwards one link at a time
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Replace "my" with the speaker and trace the path.
importantRulesAndFormulas.whenToUse: "She is my mother's only daughter" → speaker's sister (or the speaker).
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: "My father's only son" → the speaker himself

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Coded relations
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Assign each symbol a relation (for example + = mother, − = brother, × = father) and read left to right
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Write the chain, then name the final relation.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: P − R + Q: P is the brother of R, R is the mother of Q

mainNarrative: Read each statement slowly and underline the relation word and its direction. "A is the brother of B" does not say who is older or what B's gender is. Mark A as male and put A on the same level as B. Do not invent information that is not in the statement.

For a chain such as "A is the brother of B, B is the mother of C", draw B and C first (a mother and her child), place A beside B, and note that A is the brother of C's mother, which makes A the maternal uncle of C.

Pointing statements usually contain "only" to give you certainty. "My father's only son" can only be the speaker (if the speaker is male) or the speaker's brother. In "she is my mother's mother's only daughter's daughter", the only daughter of the speaker's maternal grandmother is the speaker's mother, and her daughter is the speaker's sister.

Coded relation questions use symbols for relationships. If + means mother, − means brother and × means father, then "P − R + Q" says P is the brother of R and R is the mother of Q, so P is Q's maternal uncle.
If the answer is ambiguous (a "cousin" could be male or female), the question will give an option such as "cannot be determined" or will ask only for the relation, which is cousin.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why "only" matters
deepDiveAspects.content: The word "only" removes ambiguity. "Her mother's only son" is a unique person, her brother. Without "only", you could not tell which son is meant. Whenever you see "only", use it to merge two descriptions into one person.

deepDiveAspects.title: Gender clues
deepDiveAspects.content: Unless the statement gives gender, do not guess. "Parent", "sibling", "child", "cousin" and "spouse" are neutral. The final answer should use a neutral term whenever the gender cannot be fixed from the statements.

problemVariations.description: Find the relation from a short chain.
problemVariations.exampleSnippet: A is B's brother. B is C's mother. A is C's ___?

problemVariations.description: A person points to another and describes the link.
problemVariations.exampleSnippet: She is my mother's only daughter's daughter.

problemVariations.description: Several people and relations are given.
problemVariations.exampleSnippet: A and B are a married couple; C is their son; D is C's wife.

problemVariations.description: Count the number of people of a type.
problemVariations.exampleSnippet: How many brothers does A have?

solvedExamples.title: A chain of relations
solvedExamples.question: A is the brother of B. B is the mother of C. How is A related to C?
givenInfo: A is the brother of B
B is the mother of C
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Draw B and C, then place A beside B.

steps.title: Mark the first relation
steps.explanation: A is male (brother) and is at the same level as B.

steps.title: Mark the second relation
steps.explanation: B is the mother of C, so C is one level below B.

steps.title: Read the path
steps.explanation: A is the brother of C's mother.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The brother of one's mother is the maternal uncle.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Answering "father", which would require A to be the husband of B.

solvedExamples.title: A pointing statement
solvedExamples.question: Pointing to a girl, Anil says, "She is the daughter of my mother's mother's only daughter." How is the girl related to Anil?
givenInfo: The girl = daughter of (Anil's mother's mother's only daughter)
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Work from Anil outwards, one link at a time.

steps.title: Her only daughter
steps.explanation: The only daughter of Anil's maternal grandmother is Anil's mother.

steps.title: The daughter of that person
steps.explanation: The daughter of Anil's mother is Anil's sister.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The word "only" makes the daughter of the grandmother unique: it must be Anil's mother.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Answering "cousin" by thinking the "mother's mother's daughter" is an aunt.

solvedExamples.title: Coded relation
solvedExamples.question: If A + B means A is the mother of B, A − B means A is the brother of B and A × B means A is the father of B, which expression shows that P is the maternal uncle of Q?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: A maternal uncle is the brother of the mother.

steps.title: State what is needed
steps.explanation: P must be the brother of Q's mother. Let R be Q's mother.

steps.title: Write the two relations
steps.explanation: P is the brother of R (P − R) and R is the mother of Q (R + Q).

steps.title: Join them
steps.explanation: The chain is P − R + Q.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Reading left to right: P is the brother of R and R is the mother of Q.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Writing R − P + Q, which makes R the maternal uncle.

shortcutMethods.title: Draw first, read second

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Try to keep all relations in memory and reason mentally.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Draw squares for males and circles for females, join spouses with a short horizontal line and children below. Write every new person as soon as the statement mentions them.

rulesForApplication: "My mother's brother" is the maternal uncle; "my father's sister" is the paternal aunt.
The child of an uncle or aunt is a cousin.
Resolve "only son/daughter" as a single unique person.
If the question asks "how is A related to B", read from A's perspective, not B's.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading the relation from the wrong side
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Answering how B is related to A instead of A to B.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Re-read the final question; write "A is the ___ of B" and check.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Treating "cousin" or "sibling" as male or female.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Use neutral terms unless the gender is stated.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Answering "uncle" for a mother's side but "paternal uncle" for the father's side.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Ask: did the link pass through the mother or the father?

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Adding extra siblings that the statement rules out.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Use "only" to identify a single person.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options that disagree in gender or in generation level with your tree; usually two options go at once.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Blood relation questions are easy to get right if you draw. Take 10 seconds to draw rather than 40 seconds to think.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Care with the wording of the question matters more than speed.

summaryBullets: Draw squares for males, circles for females; generations as rows.
Maternal = mother's side; paternal = father's side.
The child of an uncle or aunt is a cousin.
Use "only" to identify a unique person.
In coded relations, read the chain left to right.

keyTakeaways: Read the question from the correct person's perspective.
Chains of two or three links are enough for most questions.
selfCheckQuestions: Can I identify the relation of A to C if A is the sister of B and B is the father of C?
Can I resolve "my father's only son"?
Can I write the expression for "P is the maternal uncle of Q" using + − × symbols?
